prov.heading: Provision for credit losses
prov.text:
Management has established and maintains a methodology for determining and adjusting its allowance for credit losses based on a combination of quantitative and qualitative analysis, and changes in the required allowance are recorded through income as a provision. The quantitative portion of the model is significantly influenced by changes in projected economic conditions, as well as changes in the composition of the numerous loan portfolio segments. Qualitative adjustments reflect the degree to which management anticipates future outcomes may differ from those projected by the quantitative model.

The provision for credit losses was a credit of $2.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to provision expense of $1.1 million for the same period in the prior year. The decrease was largely due to a $2.9 million partial recovery of a commercial and industrial loan participation in the current year period, received in connection with a legal settlement. This recovery resulted in net recoveries for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaling $2.6 million, compared to net charge-offs of $0.1 million for the same period in the prior year.

net.text:
The following table presents selected financial information for the periods indicated, and the dollar and percent change (in thousands, except per share and ratio data):

The following table presents selected financial information for the periods indicated, and the dollar and percent change (in thousands, except per share and ratio data) adjusted for nonrecurring items (refer to the GAAP to Non-GAAP reconciliations, pages 82-85, for further information):

(1) Adjusted for $17.5 million loss on sale of securities available for sale and $0.6 million gain on sale of previous branch property during the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

(2) Adjusted for tax impact of loss on sale of securities available for sale and gain on sale of previous branch property during the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

The Corporation reported net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 of $12.7 million, or $2.63 per share, compared to net income of $7.8 million, or $1.62 per share, for the same period in the prior year. Return on average equity for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 18.36%, compared to 12.89% for the same period in the prior year.

ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text: The Corporation believes cash flows from operations, available cash balances, and its ability to generate cash through short-term and long-term borrowings are sufficient to fund the Corporation’s operating liquidity needs. Cash provided by operating activities in the first nine months of 2026 and 2025 primarily resulted from net income after non-cash operating adjustments.

net sales.heading: Pre-Provision Net Revenue
net sales.text: Pre-provision net revenue (“PPNR”), adjusted PPNR, and the ratios of each to average assets and average equity are non-GAAP financial measures. PPNR represents the Corporation’s income before income tax expense, excluding the provision for credit losses. Adjusted PPNR further excludes the impact of certain transactions or other material items of income or expense that may have had a disproportionate positive or negative impact on the Corporation’s financial results during a particular period. These measures are meaningful to the Corporation, as well as investors and analysts, in assessing the Corporation’s ability to generate earnings sufficient to absorb credit losses and support capital, independent of the volatility and timing of provision expense.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
The following table presents net interest income for the periods indicated, and the dollar and percent change (in thousands):

Net interest income, which is the difference between the interest income earned on interest-earning assets such as loans and securities, and the interest expense paid on interest-bearing liabilities such as deposits and borrowings, is the largest contributor to the Corporation’s earnings.

Net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $3.0 million to $25.7 million compared to the same period in the prior year, largely due to an increase of $3.1 million in interest income on loans and a decrease of $1.3 million in interest expense on deposits, partially offset by a decrease of $0.9 million in interest income on interest-earning deposits and an increase of $0.6 million in interest expense on borrowed funds.

Interest income on loans, including fees, increased to $34.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 , from $31.0 million for the same period in the prior year. The increase was mostly due to an increase of $204.6 million in average balances of total loans, as well as an increase of two basis points in the average yield on total loans.

intro.text: The Corporation was incorporated on January 2, 1985 under the laws of the State of New York and is headquartered in Elmira, New York. The Corporation was organized for the purpose of acquiring the Bank. The Bank was established in 1833 under the name Chemung Canal Bank, and was subsequently granted a New York State bank charter in 1895. In 1902, the Bank was reorganized as a New York State trust company under the name Elmira Trust Company, and its name was changed to Chemung Canal Trust Company in 1903. The Corporation became a financial holding company in June 2000. Financial holding company status provided the Corporation with the flexibility to offer an array of financial services, such as insurance products, mutual funds, and brokerage services, which provide additional sources of fee-based income and allows the Corporation to better serve its customers.
